sources.citation: Daniels, Don R. 2015. A Reconstruction of Proto-Sogeram: Phonology, Lexicon, and Morphosyntax. PhD dissertation, University of California, Santa Barbara. 1127 pp. (Mum: sec. 2.3.5 'Mum Innovations', printed pp. 93-96; research history p. 11; refs p. 1099)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing for Mum: sec. 2.3.5 gives the Mum phoneme inventory, word-final labiovelar creation, word-initial *i fortition and 'sporadic vowel centering' (penultimate-syllable *V > ɨ) with no statement on stress, accent or tone. Only stress remark in the work is p. 71 (Mand): 'Further research into the stress systems of the Sogeram languages might reveal a consistent pattern.' No Mum grammar sketch among the appendices. Names Sweeney 1994a as the (unpublished) Mum phonology.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU. Sec. 2.22.33 'The Katiati Language' (p. 60) and 2.22.36 typological features of the Josephstaal Stock (pp. 60-61).

sources.note: Nothing specific to Katiati (segmental typology only: extra alveopalatal stop and nasal, /e/ present). General note p. 6: 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.'
